notes.meaning: David asks the Lord to listen closely to his honest cry for help. He knows his cause is just and his prayer comes from a heart that is not trying to deceive God. Because he is truly sincere, he is confident the Lord will hear him.

David asks God Himself to judge the matter and clear his name. Human judges can be unfair or easily fooled, but God sees what is right without any prejudice. David wants his verdict to come straight from the court of heaven.

God examined David's heart in the quiet hours of the night and found no wicked plot. This does not mean David was sinless, but that he was sincere and free from the crimes his enemies charged him with. He had also made a firm decision to keep his speech pure and not sin with his mouth.

Many people easily slide into violence and revenge when they are attacked, but David refused to do that. He obeyed God's word and let it direct his actions so he would not walk in destructive ways. Following Scripture kept him safe from copying the sins of evil men.

David states that he has stayed firmly on God's good path. Even when circumstances were difficult, his feet did not slip into sinful deeds. Walking in God's ways requires constant reliance on God's strength so one does not stumble.

David calls out to God with complete trust that an answer is coming. He asks the Lord to lean down and listen to his words like a father listening to his child. His past experience of God's faithfulness gives him boldness to ask for help once again.

David asks the Lord to show His wonderful and loyal covenant love in an extraordinary way. God uses His mighty power to save those who turn to Him for safety against their enemies. When danger is extreme, believers look to God's special kindness to deliver them.

David asks God to protect him like the pupil of an eye, which is guarded with extreme care. He also asks to be tucked beneath God's wings, just as a mother bird covers and shelters her young chicks from harm. These gentle word pictures remind us how precious God's people are to Him.

David seeks protection because deadly enemies have gathered all around him. These attackers are cruel and will not be satisfied with anything less than taking his life. Surrounded by mortal danger, David places his soul entirely in God's hands.

The enemies chasing David have grown rich and comfortable, which has left their hearts hard and unfeeling. Because they enjoy earthly prosperity, they speak boastfully and look down on others. Their selfish wealth has made them blind to God and deaf to pity.

The pursuers follow David closely, watching every move he makes just like hunters tracking an animal. They keep their eyes fixed toward the earth to spot any footstep so they can throw him down. David feels completely hemmed in by their tireless chase.

David compares his chief enemy to a hungry lion ready to tear its prey to pieces. Like a young lion hiding in secret places, the attacker waits patiently to pounce when least expected. Against such savage hatred, only the Lord can provide real protection.

David calls on the Lord to rise up, confront the enemy face-to-face, and bring them down. He prays for God to rescue him by His own power, using His sword against the wicked. God has full authority over evil men and can stop their attacks at any moment.

David asks to be saved from worldly men whose only reward is in this present life. Such people satisfy themselves with earthly wealth, see their children enjoy plenty, and leave fortunes behind, but they have no thought of God. David wants no part in a portion that ends at death.

In contrast to worldly men, David finds his greatest happiness in seeing God's face in righteousness, which means being made right with God and living to honor Him. When he awakes from the sleep of death into God's presence, his soul will be completely satisfied. The highest joy for a believer is to behold the Lord and be made like Him forever.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars understand awaking to refer to waking up each morning from natural sleep to enjoy God's favor and guidance, rather than the final resurrection from the dead.
